pattern.crimePattern: manager silences an employee who found him skimming
pattern.notes: Uhuru Park is a setting only; fictional boat-hire business.

ob.reportedBy: Dennis Mbugua, junior attendant, Ziwani Boat Hire
ob.text: Junior attendant Dennis Mbugua reports that senior attendant Charles Maina (44) of Ziwani Boat Hire, Uhuru Park, was found dead in the boat shed at 17:05. The cash tin is missing. Several witnesses report a loud fight between the deceased and his brother that morning.

people.name: Charles Maina
people.bio: Has rented out rowing boats on the Uhuru Park lake for twelve years. Keeps the fee book himself.

image.brief: Kenyan man, mid 40s, blue work overall, sunburnt forehead, a whistle on a lanyard, honest square face, ID-photo framing

people.name: Daniel ole Sankale
people.bio: Runs the boat hire for its owner. Wears the only green overall. Has been taking money from the Sunday takings.

image.brief: Kenyan man, late 30s, tall, green work overall with a manager's badge, a clipboard, calm and helpful expression, ID-photo framing

people.name: George Maina
people.occupation: Charles's brother; mitumba trader at Gikomba
people.bio: Fought with Charles at the shed this morning about their late mother's plot. His cap was found in the shed.

image.brief: Kenyan man, early 40s, bareheaded, a mitumba trader's money belt, red-eyed with grief and anger, ID-photo framing

people.name: Dennis Mbugua
people.bio: Rents out boats and fetches the ones that drift. Found Charles.

image.brief: Kenyan young man, early 20s, blue work overall soaked to the knees, life jacket over one shoulder, shocked, ID-photo framing

people.name: Pendo Atieno
people.bio: Everyone calls her Mama Pendo. Her cart has stood by the shed for twenty years.

image.brief: Kenyan woman, mid 50s, a bright yellow sun hat, a striped apron, the strap of a cool box over her shoulder, wise amused eyes, ID-photo framing

people.name: Victor Nyamweya
people.bio: Takes instant photos of families and writes the time on the back of each print.

image.brief: Kenyan man, early 30s, a sleeveless vest with many pockets over a T-shirt, a handful of small instant photo prints fanned in one hand, a pen behind his ear, eager to help, ID-photo framing

people.name: Margaret Wangari
people.occupation: Mitumba trader, Gikomba (next stall to George)

image.brief: Kenyan woman, about 50, a second-hand puffer jacket, a money pouch belted at her waist, a headscarf, shrewd and direct, ID-photo framing

locations.name: Ziwani Boat Hire shed, Uhuru Park
locations.description: A Sunday at Uhuru Park: families on the grass, rowing boats on the green lake, music from somewhere. The boat shed is a tin-roofed hut with oars racked on the wall, a fee book on a table and, until today, a cash tin. Attendants wear blue overalls; the manager wears green.

hotspots.label: Inside the shed
hotspots.text: Charles lies by the oar rack. An oar is on the floor beside him. The report says he was struck with it. The cash-tin shelf is empty.

hotspots.label: A cap on the bench
hotspots.text: A faded red cap with a Gikomba trader's market tag sewn inside: G. MAINA.

hotspots.label: Fee book
hotspots.text: Hire tickets for the day stapled in. Turn to the back page: pencil, in Charles's hand.

hotspots.label: Mama Pendo's ice-cream cart
hotspots.text: The cart faces the shed door and the lake.

hotspots.label: The park photographer
hotspots.text: Victor sells Amani a print from this afternoon for KSh 100: 'Look in the background. I always look in the background.'

hotspots.label: Manager's office cupboard
hotspots.text: A locked cupboard. Daniel opens it when asked, slowly. Behind a box of life jackets: the cash tin.

image.brief: a tin-roofed boat-hire shed beside a green park lake in Nairobi on a sunny Sunday, rowing boats tied up, oars racked on a wall, an ice-cream cart nearby, city skyline beyond the trees, no people in focus

inside a wooden boat-hire shed by a park lake, a gap in the rack of oars on the wall, one oar lying on the plank floor, a cupboard standing open with an empty shelf, orange life jackets piled in the corner, police tape across the door, no body visible

body.label: Faded red cap. Inside: market tag 'G. MAINA'.

image.brief: a faded red baseball cap lying on a wooden bench inside a tin boat shed, a small sewn-in market name tag visible inside the band

body.front: A family of four by the lake, laughing. In the background, small: the shed door open, a man in a green overall walking away carrying a grey box.

image.brief: an instant photo print of a smiling Kenyan family by a park lake; in the blurred background a small figure in a green work overall walks away from an open tin shed carrying a grey metal box, his face turned away

body.label: Grey cash tin, ZIWANI stencilled on the lid. Empty.

image.brief: an empty grey metal cash tin with its lid open on a cupboard shelf, behind a stack of orange life jackets, a stencilled word on the lid

facts.text: Charles Maina was found dead in the boat shed at 17:05.
Witnesses say Charles had a loud fight with his brother at the shed this morning.
Charles was struck with an oar from the rack.
The cash tin is gone from its shelf.
George Maina's cap is on the bench in the shed.
Fee book: '16:00 tin count — D.S.', initialled by the manager.
Back page, Charles's pencil: 'D — 3 Sundays short.'
Mama Pendo saw George storm out of the shed bareheaded at 09:15 after shouting at Charles. He never came back.
Mama Pendo saw Charles alive in the shed doorway at 15:55.
Dennis was out on the lake fetching a drifting boat from 15:50 to 16:25. Mama Pendo watched; the children were cheering him.
Victor's print, timed 16:12: in the background, a man in a green overall leaves the shed carrying a grey box.
Victor: "Attendants wear blue. Only the manager, Daniel ole Sankale, wears green."
Victor took photos of families on the lawn from 15:30 to 17:00; his print numbers run in sequence.
Mama Pendo served ice cream at her cart all afternoon, in full view of the lake.
Gikomba neighbour: George was at his mitumba stall from 11:00 to 18:00, apart from five minutes when she watched it.
The cash tin was behind a box of life jackets in the manager's locked cupboard. Empty.
George: "I shouted at him about our mother's shamba and I left. I was at Gikomba all day."
George says he forgot his cap in the shed when he stormed out in the morning.
Daniel: "I was in the office doing the books all afternoon. I didn't hear anything."
Daniel: "The brother was screaming at him this morning. Everyone heard."
Dennis: "I was rowing out for the boat that drifted. When I came back he was on the floor."

interrogations.intro: Dennis is still wet to the knees. "I was on the water. I was on the water and he was on the floor."

topics.reply: His brother shouted at him at nine about their mother's shamba. Everyone heard. Then he left.
The manager? He was around. In and out of the office. He does the count at four.

interrogations.intro: Mama Pendo hands Amani an ice cream without asking and doesn't take money. "Twenty years I've seen that shed. Twenty years."

topics.reply: George came at nine, shouted, and stormed out with no cap, hands in the air. He never came back. I'd have seen him.
Dennis was rowing for that drifting boat from ten to four. The children were cheering. He was on the water the whole time.
The manager? He walks around a lot. I don't watch him. I watch the children near the water.

interrogations.intro: Victor flips through a stack of prints. "I write the time on every one. Customers like it. Police like it more."

topics.reply: Look in the background. Green overall. Only one man in this park wears that colour of overall.

interrogations.intro: George arrives from Gikomba, out of breath, bareheaded. "They're saying it was me. They're already saying it."

topics.reply: My cap? I left it there in the morning. I was so angry I didn't notice. Mama Pendo saw me go.
We fought about Mother's plot. He wanted to sell, I didn't. I'd give him the whole shamba to have him back.

interrogations.intro: Daniel meets Amani at the shed with a clipboard and a sympathetic face. "Terrible. The brother was here this morning, you know."

topics.reply: 'D'? Could be anyone. Dennis. Delivery men. Charles kept strange notes.
Green overall? The owner sometimes wears one. Anyone can buy an overall.

prosecutor.pass: Not the brother. The man in green, with the tin. That will hold, and I'm glad you didn't send me the brother.
fail: This doesn't hold up. A fight in the morning is not a killing in the afternoon. Where was the brother?
No. Charles wrote down who he suspected. Read the back page, then look at the background of that photo.

proof.concludes: George left at 09:15 without his cap and was in Gikomba all afternoon. The cap means nothing.
With the brother cleared, the only suspicion Charles himself wrote down was 'D': Daniel ole Sankale or Dennis Mbugua.
At 16:12 a man in the manager's green overall left the shed with a box, while Dennis was out on the water. It was Daniel.

eliminations.why: George left bareheaded at 09:15 and was at his stall in Gikomba from 11:00 to 18:00.
Dennis was out on the lake from 15:50 to 16:25, watched by Mama Pendo and a crowd of children.
Mama Pendo served ice cream at her cart all afternoon in full view of the lake.
Victor was photographing families on the lawn; his print numbers run in sequence.

reconstruction.text: For three Sundays the takings are short. Charles checks the fee book against the tin and writes in pencil: 'D — 3 Sundays short.' He tells the manager he'll report it to the owner on Monday.
09:15. George shouts at his brother about their mother's plot and storms off, leaving his cap. Everyone hears. Everyone remembers.
16:00. Daniel does the tin count. Dennis is out on the lake after a drifting boat. Daniel picks up an oar.
16:12. He walks out of the shed in his green overall with the grey tin under his arm, to make it look like a robbery. In the background of a family's photo.
That evening George collects his cap from the police. He holds it a long time before he puts it on.

tier1.line: Everyone is looking at the brother. Charles wasn't. Read what he wrote on the back page.

tier2.line: A green overall in the background of a photograph, and only one man in the park who wears green.

glossary.def: Second-hand clothes, sold in huge markets like Gikomba.
Respectful way to address an older woman; 'Mama Pendo'.

ui.beatNotes: First three-step proof. The notebook's pinned-facts tray (up to six facts) is introduced. First photograph at full size with the case-photo treatment and zoom: the green figure is only visible when zoomed into the background.
